Karlino Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Karlino, Poland

Demolished. Until 1814, Karlino's Jews were buried in Świdwin, until a royal decree that year banned transporting the deceased between cities, prompting the local community to purchase its own cemetery land. At the beginning of WWII, local farmers were ordered to remove the cemetery's tombstones for use in paving a nearby road; some reportedly refused to comply. The wall survived until the 1970s, when it was pulled down by local residents and the site leveled; in 1996, a war memorial was erected on the grounds, later incorporated into the city park in 1998.
